Warps grid-stride\n//   over the rows so any grid size covers all rows.\n//\n// Arguments: same as spmvCpu (device pointers), dim = number of rows\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\n__global__ void spmvCsrWarpKernel(const double* __restrict__ val, const index_t* __restrict__ cols,\n                                  const index_t* __restrict__ rowDelimiters,\n                                  const double* __restrict__ vec, const index_t dim,\n                                  double* __restrict__ out) {\n    const index_t lane = threadIdx.x % WARP_SIZE;\n    const index_t globalWarp = (blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x) / WARP_SIZE;\n    const index_t totalWarps = (gridDim.x * blockDim.x) / WARP_SIZE;\n\n    for (index_t row = globalWarp; I also check the build output for warnings (there are none) and confirm the out-of-tree build didn't leave stray files in the workspace. The timing discrepancy between the first run (3.7ms) and second run (0.06ms) looks like CUDA context initialization and lazy module loading overhead on the first launch, which is a real but expected cost.\n\nI decide this is worth addressing with a legitimate fix: adding a cheap, untimed warm-up kernel launch before the timed measurements so the benchmark reflects actual kernel performance rather than driver initialization overhead — a fair and honest improvement to include.\n\n","time":{"start":1793030769047,"end":1793030775976},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
